title: Optimal Search and Positive-Adversary Bounds with Accidentally Collapsing Measurements
description:
Research preprint, version 0.4.0. We study a hypothetical Born sampler that independently projects its sampled register with probability epsilon, with immediate outcome/flag feedback on the same persistent state and a noiseless input oracle. Constant-success unique-item search has optimal total query/readout/preparation/ordinary-measurement cost Theta(N^(1/3)+sqrt(epsilon N)), with separately paid gates, classical work, space, transcript bits and precision.

The retained second main theorem states: every finite Boolean promise problem with success at least 2/3 satisfies Q min{P+1,ceil(1/epsilon)} >= Adv_+(f)/36, using P+1 at epsilon=0. Adv_+ is the entrywise-nonnegative spectral adversary. A complete-history spectral query charge covers entangled workspace, partial measurements, permitted resets, feedback and unequal stopping without a history-count factor. Fixed and decreasing powers are proved separately. The parity application gives Omega(n) queries at any fixed positive collapse rate. The sharper search theorem is retained.

The algorithmic template, ideal endpoint and conditional-copy framework are attributed to ABFL and Miloschewsky--Podder; prior imperfect-readout robustness to Abbas et al.; positive weighted/spectral adversary machinery to the established literature including Miloschewsky--Podder and Spalek--Szegedy. Certificates may be exponentially large analytical objects. No signed-adversary extension, efficient certificate discovery, physical implementation, classification of all noisy PDQP or ordinary BPP/BQP result is claimed. OpenAI Codex assisted derivation, literature comparison, drafting and internal checking. Separate provider CLI AI-review reports and dispositions are archived; no independent human peer review or formal certification has occurred.

Version 0.4.0 adds an auxiliary whole-transcript implementation-error theorem: TV <= min{1,sqrt(K) sum_j delta_j + P tau}, with K=min{P+1,ceil(1/epsilon)} (P+1 at zero), uniform ordinary-gate operator-norm errors delta_j and separately coupled collapse-rate error tau for an identical frozen policy. The bound preserves arbitrary workspace, partial measurements, immediate feedback and unequal stopping, with no dimension, branch-count or inverse branch-probability factor. Explicit gate-precision, success, description-evaluation, compilation, synthesis, repetition, memory and transcript costs are included. It is an attributed consequence of the existing power comparisons; ABFL gate-set independence, Cakan et al. conditional-copy continuity and Dawson--Nielsen synthesis are acknowledged. No general ambient-noise or physical-implementation claim is made.
